meta.note: Demo dataset. Listings, operating hours and reviews are illustrative samples for demonstration purposes — confirm details before visiting.
meta.verified_note: verified=true listings are venues confirmed to exist. verified=false listings are indicative entries (mall food courts, chain outlets) whose exact outlet is not confirmed.

eateries.name: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice
eateries.address: 1 Kadayanallur St, #01-10/11 Maxwell Food Centre, Singapore 069184
eateries.description: A Maxwell Food Centre institution serving silky poached chicken over fragrant rice, with a queue that moves faster than it looks.

reviews.author: Marcus L.
reviews.text: Chicken was tender and the rice properly fragrant. Go before noon to beat the queue.

reviews.author: Priya S.
reviews.text: Reliable plate of chicken rice. Chilli packs a real punch — ask for extra.

eateries.name: Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle
eateries.description: Michelin-listed bak chor mee with springy noodles, vinegary chilli and a generous hand with liver and pork slices.

reviews.author: Wei Jie T.
reviews.text: Worth the wait. The vinegar and chilli balance is exactly right and the liver is cooked perfectly.

reviews.author: Aisha R.
reviews.text: Small stall, big flavour. Portion is modest for the price but the noodles are excellent.

eateries.name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh
eateries.description: Peppery Teochew-style pork rib soup served in a shophouse, with free soup refills and crisp you tiao on the side.

reviews.author: Daniel K.
reviews.text: Rich pepper broth and ribs that fall off the bone. The refill policy keeps the whole table happy.

reviews.author: Nurul H.
reviews.text: Comforting on a rainy evening. Gets busy around 7pm, so come early.

eateries.name: Jumbo Seafood (Riverside Point)
eateries.description: Riverside seafood house known for chilli crab with fried mantou, plus black pepper crab and a lively evening crowd.

reviews.author: Elaine C.
reviews.text: The chilli crab sauce is the star — order extra mantou to mop it all up. Great river view too.

reviews.author: Tom B.
reviews.text: Pricey but a solid spot for a celebration. Book ahead on weekends.

eateries.name: Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow
eateries.address: 51 Old Airport Rd, #01-121 Old Airport Road Food Centre, Singapore 390051
eateries.description: Wok hei-heavy char kway teow with cockles and Chinese sausage, from one of the east side's best-loved hawker stalls.

reviews.author: Kai Siong L.
reviews.text: Smoky, savoury and not too oily. One of the better plates in the east.

reviews.author: Grace W.
reviews.text: Worth queuing for. Ask for extra cockles if that is your thing.

eateries.name: Tim Ho Wan (Jewel Changi)
eateries.address: 78 Airport Blvd, #02-223 Jewel Changi Airport, Singapore 819666
eateries.description: Dim sum chain famous for its baked BBQ pork buns with a crackly sugar crust, handy before or after a flight.

reviews.author: Rachel N.
reviews.text: The pork buns alone are worth the trip. Crisp outside, sweet-savoury inside.

reviews.author: Hafiz A.
reviews.text: Convenient location and quick service. Slightly pricey for dim sum but consistent.

eateries.name: Hajjah Maimunah
eateries.description: Nasi padang spread over two shophouses, with rendang, soto ayam and tahu telur drawing a steady lunch crowd.

reviews.author: Siti Z.
reviews.text: Rendang is deeply flavoured and the vegetables are not an afterthought. Great value.

reviews.author: Jonathan P.
reviews.text: Arrive early — the popular dishes sell out. Tahu telur is a must.

eateries.name: Warong Nasi Pariaman
eateries.description: Old-school Minang nasi padang with dry gulai, grilled chicken and a queue of regulars who know exactly what to order.

reviews.author: Farah I.
reviews.text: The gulai here tastes like someone's grandmother is in the kitchen. Generous portions.

reviews.author: Chin H.
reviews.text: Fast, friendly and filling. Go easy on the sambal unless you are brave.

eateries.name: Geylang Serai Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: A one-stop Malay food hall: mee rebus, mee siam, satay and nasi padang all under one roof, plus a wet market downstairs.

reviews.author: Amir R.
reviews.text: Mee rebus gravy was thick and slightly sweet — exactly what I wanted. Plenty of seating at lunch.

reviews.author: Melissa T.
reviews.text: Brilliant variety. Come hungry and share a few plates between friends.

eateries.name: Selera Rasa Nasi Lemak
eateries.address: 2 Adam Rd, #01-02 Adam Road Food Centre, Singapore 289876
eateries.description: Coconut-rich rice, crisp fried chicken and sweet-savoury sambal — a breakfast queue that is practically a Singapore ritual.

reviews.author: Benny O.
reviews.text: The rice is fragrant and the chicken stays crunchy under the sambal. Worth the morning queue.

reviews.author: Nadia K.
reviews.text: Classic plate done well. The otah is a good add-on.

eateries.name: Muthu's Curry
eateries.description: Long-running banana-leaf restaurant best known for fish head curry and rich, coconut-forward curries.

reviews.author: Deepak V.
reviews.text: Fish head curry is tangy and generous — easily feeds three. Banana leaf rice is a must.

reviews.author: Sarah L.
reviews.text: Bold flavours and quick service. It gets loud and busy at dinner, which is part of the fun.

eateries.name: Zam Zam Restaurant
eateries.description: A century-old murtabak specialist opposite the mosque, with tissue-thin roti and towering portions.

reviews.author: Arun M.
reviews.text: Murtabak is crisp at the edges and packed with filling. One is enough for two people.

reviews.author: Lisa G.
reviews.text: No-frills and fast. The mutton murtabak with curry on the side is the move.

eateries.name: Komala Vilas
eateries.description: Vegetarian South Indian canteen serving crisp thosai, idli and unlimited banana-leaf rice since 1947.

reviews.author: Vikram S.
reviews.text: Thosai is crisp and the chutneys are fresh. Simple, cheap and satisfying.

reviews.author: Anna W.
reviews.text: Great vegetarian option in Little India. The meal set is excellent value.

eateries.name: Springleaf Prata Place
eateries.address: 438 Upper Bukit Timah Rd, #01-01 The Rail Mall, Singapore 678055
eateries.description: Modern prata cafe with creative fillings alongside the classics — plaster prata, murtabak and fragrant curries.

reviews.author: Hui Ling C.
reviews.text: Prata is flaky and the fish curry is properly spiced. Good supper spot.

reviews.author: Ravi N.
reviews.text: The plaster prata is a guilty pleasure. Friendly staff even at closing time.

eateries.name: PS.Cafe (Harding Road)
eateries.description: Leafy Dempsey brunch spot known for truffle fries, hearty burgers and a very pleasant patio.

reviews.author: Cheryl T.
reviews.text: Truffle fries are still the benchmark. Sit outside if the weather is kind.

reviews.author: Mark D.
reviews.text: Solid brunch with generous portions. Service can slow down on weekend mornings.

eateries.name: Wild Honey
eateries.description: All-day breakfast restaurant plating breakfasts from around the world, from eggs Benedict to fluffy pancakes.

reviews.author: Janelle L.
reviews.text: Pancakes were fluffy and the portions generous. Perfect slow weekend breakfast.

reviews.author: Owen F.
reviews.text: Great eggs Benedict and good coffee. Expect a wait for tables at brunch.

eateries.name: Merci Marcel (Tiong Bahru)
eateries.description: French-inspired bistro and wine bar with a cheese counter, pasta and a charming neighbourhood patio.

reviews.author: Camille R.
reviews.text: Feels like a proper neighbourhood bistro. Cheese selection is excellent and the staff know it well.

reviews.author: Derek Y.
reviews.text: Lovely space and good pasta. A bit pricey but great for a relaxed dinner.

eateries.name: Sarnies
eateries.description: Cafe in a heritage shophouse serving generous sandwiches, all-day brunch and properly strong coffee.

reviews.author: Rina P.
reviews.text: Coffee is consistently good and the sandwiches are hefty. Good CBD lunch escape.

reviews.author: Alex M.
reviews.text: Busy at lunch but service keeps up. The breakfast plate is my usual order.

eateries.name: Keisuke Tonkotsu King
eateries.description: Cult-favourite tonkotsu ramen shop with rich broth, free egg and beansprouts, and a queue that starts before opening.

reviews.author: Yuki T.
reviews.text: Broth is thick and deeply savoury without being overwhelming. Free egg is a nice touch.

reviews.author: Sharon K.
reviews.text: Excellent ramen, tiny shop. Go off-peak or be ready to queue.

eateries.name: Ramen Nagi (ION Orchard)
eateries.description: Customisable ramen bowls with a fiery red king and rich butao broth, tucked inside ION Orchard.

reviews.author: Hiroshi N.
reviews.text: Rich broth and a good level of spice in the Red King. Noodles have a nice bite.

reviews.author: Michelle C.
reviews.text: Fun to customise your bowl. Gets crowded at dinner but the queue moves.

eateries.name: Sushi Tei (Raffles City)
eateries.address: 252 North Bridge Rd, #03-002 Raffles City, Singapore 179103
eateries.description: Dependable conveyor-belt sushi chain with a wide menu of sashimi, bento sets and cooked dishes.

reviews.author: Wei Ming H.
reviews.text: Reliable sushi at a fair price. The salmon sashimi is fresh and generously cut.

reviews.author: Claire B.
reviews.text: Good family option in the mall. Bento sets are decent value.

eateries.name: Man Man Japanese Unagi Restaurant
eateries.description: Unagi specialist grilling freshwater eel to order, served over rice in lacquered boxes or as hitsumabushi.

reviews.author: Kenneth W.
reviews.text: Eel is grilled beautifully — crisp skin, soft flesh. The hitsumabushi set is worth it.

reviews.author: Aiko S.
reviews.text: Tastes like Tokyo. Small space, so book ahead for dinner.

eateries.name: Todamgol
eateries.description: Cosy Korean BBQ and stew house with charcoal grills, banchan refills and a lively dinner atmosphere.

reviews.author: Jae H.
reviews.text: Proper Korean BBQ with good cuts and plenty of banchan. Staff help with the grilling.

reviews.author: Tanya L.
reviews.text: Kimchi stew was bubbling hot and full of pork. Smoky clothes afterwards, but worth it.

eateries.name: Kko Kko Nara
eateries.description: Korean fried chicken and late-night stews, with crispy double-fried wings and a generous army stew.

reviews.author: Dong W.
reviews.text: Chicken stays crunchy even with sauce. Perfect late-night food.

reviews.author: Priyanka G.
reviews.text: Army stew is huge and great for sharing. Service is fast even when full.

eateries.name: SBCD Korean Tofu House
eateries.description: Bubbling sundubu jjigae sets with purple rice, banchan and a choice of spice level — quick and comforting.

reviews.author: Mei Lin S.
reviews.text: Stew arrives boiling and the tofu is silky. Good value set with rice and banchan.

reviews.author: Ethan C.
reviews.text: Comfort food done right. Ask for mild if you are not used to Korean heat.

eateries.name: Newton Food Centre
eateries.description: Sprawling hawker centre known for satay, BBQ seafood and oyster omelette, bustling late into the night.

reviews.author: Gareth T.
reviews.text: Satay stalls are the highlight. Come with a group so you can order across several stalls.

reviews.author: Serena H.
reviews.text: Lively and a bit chaotic, which is half the fun. Oyster omelette was crisp and generous.

eateries.name: Satay by the Bay
eateries.description: Open-air satay garden beside the Supertrees, with smoky skewers, BBQ chicken wings and cold drinks.

reviews.author: Nina A.
reviews.text: Satay is smoky and the peanut sauce is generous. Nice spot for an evening walk afterwards.

reviews.author: Bryan L.
reviews.text: A little touristy but convenient and tasty. Chicken wings are a good side.

eateries.name: 328 Katong Laksa
eateries.description: Peranakan-style laksa with thick coconut gravy and short-cut noodles, eaten with a spoon and plenty of chilli.

reviews.author: Lena K.
reviews.text: Gravy is thick and coconutty, and the cockles are fresh. Proper Katong laksa.

reviews.author: Sam R.
reviews.text: Simple menu, done well. Add otah and a lime juice.

eateries.name: Tiong Bahru Bakery
eateries.description: French bakery famous for flaky croissants and kouign-amann, with pavement seating in a heritage neighbourhood.

reviews.author: Chloe D.
reviews.text: Croissants are shatteringly crisp. The kouign-amann is dangerously good.

reviews.author: Ibrahim S.
reviews.text: Great pastries and coffee. Weekend mornings are busy but the queue is manageable.

eateries.name: Ah Chew Desserts
eateries.description: Traditional Cantonese dessert shop with mango sago, chendol and tau suan — a refreshing stop after a Liang Seah meal.

reviews.author: Wen Qi O.
reviews.text: Mango sago is cold, creamy and not too sweet. Exactly what a hot evening needs.

reviews.author: Daphne L.
reviews.text: Classic dessert shop with a big menu. Chendol is generous with the gula melaka.

eateries.name: Chong Pang Nasi Lemak
eateries.description: A Yishun supper stalwart: coconut rice, crisp fried chicken and sambal, served late into the night.

reviews.author: Wei J.
reviews.text: The queue moves quickly and the fried chicken is still hot at midnight. Best late-night plate in the north.

reviews.author: Hafiz M.
reviews.text: Rice is fragrant and the sambal has a proper kick. Parking around Chong Pang is the only hassle.

eateries.name: White Restaurant (Sembawang)
eateries.description: The original Sembawang white bee hoon — silky rice vermicelli in a light seafood broth, best shared.

reviews.author: Serena K.
reviews.text: White bee hoon is worth the trip north. Broth is sweet with seafood and not overly heavy.

reviews.author: Daniel T.
reviews.text: Come in a group so you can order the crab too. Gets very busy on weekends.

eateries.name: Chomp Chomp Food Centre
eateries.description: Serangoon Garden's open-air hawker centre, famous for satay, hokkien mee and barbecue chicken wings after dark.

reviews.author: Cheryl N.
reviews.text: Satay and chicken wings are the classics here. Go early — the good stalls sell out.

reviews.author: Marcus H.
reviews.text: Loud, crowded and exactly what you want from a hawker centre at night. Bring tissues.

eateries.name: Lola's Cafe (Kovan)
eateries.description: A neighbourhood all-day cafe off Kovan: eggs, pancakes and coffee in a bright, easy-going room.

reviews.author: Amelia W.
reviews.text: Pancakes were fluffy and the coffee is properly good. No rush to leave, which is rare.

reviews.author: Ryan C.
reviews.text: Solid brunch spot if you're in the north-east. Weekend waits are real, so go early.

eateries.name: Boon Lay Place Market & Food Village
eateries.description: A Boon Lay hawker centre with a famous nasi lemak stall and a queue before it opens, plus noodles, porridge and fried sides across the other stalls.

reviews.author: Nurul A.
reviews.text: The nasi lemak stall still has the best sambal in the west. Rice is warm even mid-morning.

reviews.author: Kelvin L.
reviews.text: Come before 8am for the nasi lemak without a long queue. Plenty of other stalls too.

eateries.name: Taman Jurong Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: A big, unpretentious western-Singapore hawker centre with noodles, laksa and fried fish soup across two floors.

reviews.author: Gerald S.
reviews.text: Plenty of seats and prices are low. Laksa is a good bowl for the money.

reviews.author: Pei Ling C.
reviews.text: Nothing fancy, just honest hawker food. Go before the lunch crowd.

eateries.name: Bedok 85 Fengshan Food Centre
eateries.description: A Bedok supper institution: bak chor mee, satay and barbecue seafood under one noisy roof.

reviews.author: Wei Ming
reviews.text: Bak chor mee here is the reason to come. Go after 8pm when every stall is running.

reviews.author: Farah
reviews.text: Satay is well marinated and cheap. Seating is tight but turnover is fast.

eateries.name: Changi Village Hawker Centre
eateries.description: The place for nasi lemak by the sea, plus wanton mee and satay, a short walk from the ferry terminal.

reviews.author: Nadia
reviews.text: Came off the boat hungry and the nasi lemak delivered. Rice is properly coconutty.

reviews.author: Jun Hao
reviews.text: Long queue for the famous stall but it moves. Eat outside facing the water.

eateries.name: East Coast Lagoon Food Village
eateries.description: Seaside hawker centre in East Coast Park, known for satay, otah and barbecue chicken wings at sunset.

reviews.author: Divya
reviews.text: Satay with the sea breeze is hard to beat. Bring cash for most stalls.

reviews.author: Terence
reviews.text: Otah is freshly grilled and smoky. Parking fills up on weekend evenings.

eateries.name: Tampines Round Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: A big heartland hawker centre with solid char kway teow, laksa and fish soup at breakfast time.

reviews.author: Shuhui
reviews.text: Char kway teow has good wok hei and the queue is reasonable before 9am.

reviews.author: Bala
reviews.text: Laksa is creamy without being cloying. Plenty of tables at mid-morning.

eateries.name: Alibabab Eating House (Katong)
eateries.description: A Katong prata house that runs late, with crisp roti prata, murtabak and teh tarik.

reviews.author: Arun
reviews.text: Prata is crisp at the edges and soft inside. Ask for extra curry.

reviews.author: Michelle
reviews.text: Murtabak is generous and the tea is properly strong. Good late-night stop.

eateries.name: Kim Choo Kueh Chang (Katong)
eateries.description: Peranakan rice dumplings, kueh and laksa in a shophouse on East Coast Road.

reviews.author: Grace
reviews.text: Bak chang is properly wrapped and the laksa is the real deal. Lovely shophouse.

reviews.author: Hock Seng
reviews.text: Bought kueh to take home and they were gone by evening. Buy double.

eateries.name: Marine Parade Hawker Centre
eateries.description: Neighbourhood hawker centre a step from the beach, strong on noodles and porridge in the morning.

reviews.author: Adeline
reviews.text: Wanton mee is springy and the char siew is decent for the price.

reviews.author: Kumar
reviews.text: Quiet on weekday mornings, which is when I like it.

eateries.name: Clementi 448 Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: Clementi's busiest food centre: fish soup, char kway teow and cheap breakfast sets.

reviews.author: Joanne
reviews.text: Fish soup is clear and sweet. Queue is long but the stall is quick.

reviews.author: Ravi
reviews.text: Char kway teow here is properly smoky. Hard to find a seat at lunch.

eateries.name: West Coast Market Square
eateries.description: A west-side food centre near the market, with noodles, porridge and roast meats.

reviews.author: Cheryl
reviews.text: Roast duck rice is generous and well priced. Seating is easy off-peak.

reviews.author: Mohan
reviews.text: Solid everyday hawker food. The hokkien mee stall is the pick.

eateries.name: Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: A Jurong West market with nasi lemak, mee rebus and BBQ seafood stalls upstairs.

reviews.author: Siti
reviews.text: Nasi lemak is cheap and generous, and the sambal is properly spicy.

reviews.author: Daryl
reviews.text: Mee rebus is a solid bowl for the money. Gets busy on Sunday mornings.

eateries.name: Bukit Batok 155 Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: A neighbourhood food centre serving laksa, wanton mee and fish soup to the Bukit Batok crowd.

reviews.author: Hwee Ling
reviews.text: Laksa is a good size and reasonably priced. Clean and airy for a hawker centre.

reviews.author: Sam
reviews.text: Wanton mee is the standout. Go early — the good stalls close by 2pm.

eateries.name: Choa Chu Kang 302 Food Centre
eateries.address: Blk 302 Choa Chu Kang Ave 4, Singapore 680302
eateries.description: A heartland food centre with nasi padang, roti prata and mee goreng through the day.

reviews.author: Zul
reviews.text: Nasi padang lauk is fresh and the prices are fair. Beef rendang is excellent.

reviews.author: Bryan
reviews.text: Prata is crisp and the curry is thick. Good breakfast spot in CCK.

eateries.name: Jurong Point (Food Court)
eateries.description: Food outlets at Jurong Point, a Singapore mall — the exact stalls vary; listing is indicative rather than a specific confirmed outlet.

reviews.author: Mabel
reviews.text: Convenient when it rains. Chicken rice stall is reliable and quick.

reviews.author: Arjun
reviews.text: Not glamorous but everything is under one roof and air-conditioned.

eateries.name: Pandan Gardens Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: A quiet west-side market food centre, good for breakfast noodles and kaya toast.

reviews.author: Serene
reviews.text: Cheap and cheerful. Kaya toast set is my weekday breakfast.

reviews.author: Patrick
reviews.text: Very local, very quiet. The laksa stall is worth the walk.

eateries.name: Teban Gardens Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: A small west-side market food centre with nasi lemak, mee rebus and fried bee hoon.

reviews.author: Hairul
reviews.text: Nasi lemak is good value and the rice is fresh in the morning.

reviews.author: Wendy
reviews.text: Mee rebus is a comforting bowl. Seats are easy to find before 9am.

eateries.name: Marsiling Mall Hawker Centre
eateries.description: A tidy air-conditioned hawker centre in Marsiling with noodles, roast meats and dessert.

reviews.author: Liyana
reviews.text: Air-conditioned hawker food is a win in the north. Char kway teow has good wok hei.

reviews.author: Wei
reviews.text: Clean, cheap and never too crowded on weekdays.

eateries.name: Woodlands Centre Road Food Centre
eateries.description: Woodlands' classic food centre by the checkpoint, known for nasi lemak and mee rebus.

reviews.author: Shafiq
reviews.text: Nasi lemak is spot on and the queue moves fast before 8am.

reviews.author: Irene
reviews.text: Mee rebus is thick and sweet. Handy if you're heading across the border.

eateries.name: Yishun 925 Hainanese Chicken Rice
eateries.description: A Yishun coffee-shop stalwart serving silky chicken rice with a punchy chilli.

reviews.author: Jia Hui
reviews.text: Chicken is silky and the rice is fragrant. Go before noon to avoid the queue.

reviews.author: Alex
reviews.text: Solid plate of chicken rice and the chilli is genuinely hot. Cheap too.

eateries.name: Chong Pang Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: The market food centre behind Chong Pang, busy from dawn with noodles, porridge and roast meats.

reviews.author: Kelvin
reviews.text: Roast duck rice is the one. Very busy on weekend mornings.

reviews.author: Priya
reviews.text: Good honest hawker breakfast. Prices are the lowest in the area.

eateries.name: Sembawang Hills Food Centre
eateries.description: A leafy food centre near Upper Thomson with char kway teow, carrot cake and fish soup.

reviews.author: Geraldine
reviews.text: Carrot cake is crisp and generously portioned. Nice breezy setting.

reviews.author: Hafeez
reviews.text: Solid neighbourhood food centre. Fish soup is the pick of the stalls.

eateries.name: Hougang 105 Hainanese Village Centre
eateries.description: A Hougang market and food centre famous for carrot cake, char kway teow and fish soup.

reviews.author: Melody
reviews.text: Carrot cake here is crispy, generous and nearly always sold out by lunch.

reviews.author: Aziz
reviews.text: Char kway teow is smoky and cheap. Go early on weekends.

eateries.name: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre
eateries.address: Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, Singapore 560628
eateries.description: A big Ang Mo Kio food centre with satay, hokkien mee and roti prata across its stalls.

reviews.author: Wenjie
reviews.text: Satay and hokkien mee both solid and cheap. Always a seat somewhere.

reviews.author: Lavanya
reviews.text: Roti prata stall does a proper crispy prata. Good breakfast stop.

eateries.name: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: The daytime half of the Serangoon Garden food scene, strong on noodles and roast meats.

reviews.author: Shaun
reviews.text: Roast duck rice is excellent for the price. Busy at breakfast.

reviews.author: Yvonne
reviews.text: Char kway teow is the standard-bearer here. Come before 11am.

eateries.name: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: Kovan's market food centre with satay, mee siam and a well-loved fried kway teow stall.

reviews.author: Benedict
reviews.text: Satay is properly charred and the peanut sauce is thick.

reviews.author: Hana
reviews.text: Mee siam is tangy and generous. Good variety for a small centre.

eateries.name: Punggol Settlement Food Court
eateries.description: Food court at the end of Punggol Point, popular for a seafood dinner before a waterfront walk.

reviews.author: Zhi Wei
reviews.text: Handy stop after cycling. Seafood is fine and the view at dusk is the draw.

reviews.author: Alethea
reviews.text: Busy at weekends. Satay is decent and cheap.

eateries.name: Casuarina Curry (Upper Thomson)
eateries.description: A prata institution on Casuarina Road: crisp roti prata, thosai and murtabak, open late.

reviews.author: Ashwin
reviews.text: The reference point for prata in Singapore. Coin prata is worth the extra.

reviews.author: Tracy
reviews.text: Thosai is crisp and the sambar is good. Crowded on weekend mornings.

eateries.name: Katong Shopping Centre Food Centre
eateries.description: A basement food centre under Katong Shopping Centre, handy for a quick laksa or chicken rice.

reviews.author: Wei Ling
reviews.text: Convenient basement stop in Katong. Laksa is decent and cheap.

reviews.author: Farhan
reviews.text: Chicken rice stall is reliable. Gets busy at lunch.

eateries.name: Bedok 216 Market & Food Centre
eateries.description: A big Bedok market food centre, strong on porridge, noodles and roast meats.

reviews.author: Hock Liang
reviews.text: Porridge is silky and the queue moves quickly. Cheap breakfast.

reviews.author: Neo
reviews.text: Wanton mee and roast duck both good. Loads of seating.

eateries.name: Tampines Mall (Food Court)
eateries.description: Food outlets at Tampines Mall, a Singapore mall — the exact stalls vary; listing is indicative rather than a specific confirmed outlet.

reviews.author: Celine
reviews.text: Convenient mall option. Air-conditioned and quick.

reviews.author: Marcus
reviews.text: Standard food court fare. Fine for a quick lunch.

eateries.name: Bukit Timah Plaza (Food Court)
eateries.description: Food outlets at Bukit Timah Plaza, a Singapore mall — the exact stalls vary; listing is indicative rather than a specific confirmed outlet.

reviews.author: Andrea
reviews.text: Handy after grocery shopping. Mixed rice is the best value here.

reviews.author: Isaac
reviews.text: Nothing exciting but convenient and clean.

eateries.name: Clementi Mall (Food Court)
eateries.description: Food outlets at Clementi Mall, a Singapore mall — the exact stalls vary; listing is indicative rather than a specific confirmed outlet.

reviews.author: Yuting
reviews.text: Prata stall opens early which is handy before work.

reviews.author: Ramesh
reviews.text: Good value and lots of seating. Gets crowded at lunch.
